notes: W15 push, steady-state. Clean, strong day — no shoulder pain anywhere ('felt super strong'). Push press ran FIRST this week and the user switched to a fast-drive tempo (not slow eccentric): 45x8/10/8, back in the 8-10 range vs W14's second-slot 7/6/6 — but order AND tempo both changed, so it's not a clean single-variable read. Farmer carry (spotlight) done at 50lb pair x ~60s x3 — 'no shoulder worries at all, hardest part was grip,' set it down on the last walk when grip failed: the shoulder stays neutral even with grip maxed.

exercises.notes: **165 cratered to 6 on genuine slow eccentrics — well below W14's 165x10/9.** User dropped to 145 (6, then 7 after rest). User's own read: 'i'm just weak lol.' **The shoulder-management win held: 'pec and shoulder were fairly quiet'** — no right-pec referral flagged this session (vs the W12-W14 set-1 referral). Cable column 30, all sets, **pain-free for the second straight week** (W14D1 was the first pain-free lateral raise in ~6 weeks). User: 'this is a good weight for me i think without wrecking the shoulder.' Holding 30 is working — don't chase load.

sets.notes: 'Absolutely can’t anymore... no matter how hard i try.'

exercises.notes: Cable column 120, reps fell 12/8/6 — **'really really hard today... have never been so hard before,'** down from W14's 120x10x3. Harder than usual this session; pairs with the chest press crater (both came after the two presses ran first). Hold 120, watch next week. **Naming: confirm with the user this is the straight-arm pulldown, not the pull-day lat pulldown** — 120 on the cable column matches the straight-arm working number exactly.

sets.notes: Had to put it down before the end — grip gave out, not the shoulder.

exercises.notes: **Spotlight reflection answered: grip was the limiter, the shoulder a non-issue.** 50lb pair (top of the prescribed 40-50), 3 walks of ~1 min (longer than the prescribed 30-45s). User: 'no shoulder worries at all, hardest part was grip' — had to set it down on the last walk when grip failed. So at 50lb / ~60s the right shoulder stays neutral even with the grip maxed out — grip pressure is NOT touching the shoulder here, the cleanest answer to the spotlight question.

shoulderStatus: **Clean push day — no pain reported anywhere.** Cable lateral raise explicitly pain-free for the second straight week ('no pain! good weight without wrecking the shoulder'). Chest press 'pec and shoulder were fairly quiet' — no right-pec set-1 referral this session, unlike W12-W14. Pull-up greasing set 'surprisingly strong... didn't feel like a noodle.' This continues the pattern that push days have stayed clean; the W14D3 flare was pull-day-volume-specific. The protective behind-back shrug was added to the push warmup this week (newly scattered here) — not separately confirmed done, but the push-day shoulder report is clean either way. Farmer carry (spotlight) confirmed zero shoulder issue at 50lb even with the grip maxed — grip was the limiter, not the shoulder.
lessonsForFutureWeeks: **Push press recovered to 8/10/8 at 45 — but two variables changed.** It ran FIRST this week AND the user used a fast-drive tempo instead of slow eccentrics ('way easier'). Vs W14's second-slot, slow-eccentric 7/6/6. Can't pin the recovery on order alone. For W16: support running push press early, and treat tempo (fast-drive vs slow-eccentric) as the user's explicit energy lever, not a fixed prescription.

**Chest press 165 cratered to 6 on genuine slow eccentrics** (vs W14's 165x10/9), then 145x6/7. User: 'i'm just weak lol.' Pec/shoulder stayed quiet (the win). Don't draw a conclusion from one session — re-check W16. If 165 craters again on slow eccentrics, talk through whether the slow tempo at 165 is the right call or whether to drop the load slightly to keep the tempo honest.

**Straight-arm pulldown (user's 'lat pulldown') fell to 120x12/8/6, 'never been so hard'** (W14 was 120x10x3). Harder this week, likely compounded by both presses running first. Hold 120; watch W16. Confirm the naming with the user so the log doesn't read as a pull-day lat pulldown.
**Cable lateral raise column 30 — second consecutive pain-free week.** Hold 30; the shoulder-up-to-strength call is landing.

**Push day stays shoulder-clean.** The flare pattern remains pull-day-volume-specific. Protective shrug now in the push warmup — keep confirming it's actually getting done since the whole point is it's easy to forget.

**Farmer carry reflection answered: grip is the limiter, shoulder stays neutral.** 50lb pair, ~60s walks, put it down on the last set when grip failed — 'no shoulder worries at all.' At 50lb the grip is the trainable edge with no shoulder risk. W16: hold 50lb and chase hold-time, or treat grip directly as the progression.
